Interface JsonElement

All Superinterfaces:
Serializable
All Known Subinterfaces:
JsonCollection
All Known Implementing Classes:
JsonArray, JsonBoolean, JsonNull, JsonNumber, JsonObject, JsonString
public interface JsonElement extends Serializable
Represents any JSON element.

    • path

      default JsonElement path(String name)
      Resolves a single child path segment from this JSON element.

      The default behavior is non-throwing and returns JsonNull.INSTANCE when the segment cannot be resolved.

      Concrete implementations may interpret the segment according to their structure, for example, object property names.

      Parameters:
      name - the path segment to resolve
      Returns:
      the resolved child element, or JsonNull.INSTANCE when the segment cannot be resolved

    • path

      default JsonElement path(int index)
      Resolves a single child path segment from this JSON element by array index.

      The default behavior is non-throwing and returns JsonNull.INSTANCE when the segment cannot be resolved.

      Parameters:
      index - the array index to resolve
      Returns:
      the resolved child element, or JsonNull.INSTANCE when the index cannot be resolved

    • decode

      <T> T decode(Type type, Type elementType)
      Converts this JSON element to a parameterized Java type.

      This overload is primarily used for collection-like structures where the raw type and the element type must both be provided.

      Type Parameters:
      T - the target Java type
      Parameters:
      type - the target raw Java type
      elementType - the generic element type associated with type
      Returns:
      the converted Java object

    • unwrap

      Object unwrap()
      Converts this JSON element to its natural Java representation.

      Implementations should return the closest Java structural equivalent of the JSON value: strings as String, numbers as Number, booleans as Boolean, arrays as List, objects as Map, and null for JSON null.

      Returns:
      the natural Java representation of this JSON element

    • wrap

      static JsonElement wrap(Object obj) throws ConversionException
      Wraps a naturally representable Java value as a JsonElement.

      Accepted inputs are: null, JsonElement, String, Number, Boolean, Map, Collection, and object arrays.

      Any other type is rejected with a ConversionException.

      Parameters:
      obj - the Java value to wrap
      Returns:
      the wrapped JsonElement
      Throws:
      ConversionException - when the value is not naturally representable as JSON

    • encode

      static JsonElement encode(Object obj) throws ConversionException
      Creates a JsonElement representation for the specified object.

      Resolution follows this order: null values become JsonNull; JsonElement values are returned as-is; booleans, numbers and strings become their respective JSON scalar types; collections and object arrays become JsonArray;

      If none of the cases above apply and the object class declares a no-argument constructor, this method falls back to reflective field-based conversion, producing a JsonObject from the non-static, non-null fields of the object.

      This reflective conversion is a convenience fallback. It should not be treated as a stable domain mapping contract for arbitrary object types.

      Parameters:
      obj - the object to be converted
      Returns:
      a JsonElement representing the specified object
      Throws:
      ConversionException

    • render

      static JsonElement render(Object obj)
      Creates a human-oriented JsonElement representation for the specified object.

      Resolution follows this order: null values become UNDEFINED; JsonElement values are returned as-is; numbers become JsonNumber; collections and object arrays become formatted JsonArray values;

      For other object types, this method falls back to a JsonString built from Renderer.render(Object).

      This method still returns a JsonElement, but it may favor readability over faithful reconstruction of the original object.

      Parameters:
      obj - the object to be formatted
      Returns:
      a human-oriented JsonElement representing the specified object
